title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1 close: illuminating/exciting grace is not the Grace of Christ Orthodoxy pressed — that grace creates the good will; received grace is not wage of a non-resisting will
pass_a_gloss: To what end so many things concerning the grace of Christ? That it may be understood that, From the common consent of the Orthodox, that illuminating, admonishing, and exciting grace, which is wanting unto no mortal (if we believe the Arminians) and which in very many lacks a saving effect, is not that grace of Christ unto whose acknowledgment the Orthodox willed to drive Pelagius; but that which creates the good will, sanctifies the man, and at length infallibly produces the effect of salvation. That this is the sense of this word was not hidden from the Master of the Sentences, lib. 2. dist. 26. lit. D. Grace, he says, preventing and preparing the will, is faith with love. This grace also Aquinas understood, 1. 2. qu. 111. art. 3. when he assigned five effects unto it, namely, that the soul be healed, that it will the good, that it work the good it wills, that it persevere in the good, that it arrive unto glory. Let this therefore remain fixed and established, that the received Grace of Christ is not the wage of a non-resisting will, but that the non-resisting will is the effect of this grace given and received. And these things abundantly suffice unto the unfolding of the first proposition.
pass_b_english: Why so much on the grace of Christ? So it is clear from Orthodox common consent: the illuminating, warning, exciting grace that—if Arminians are believed—fails no mortal, yet in many lacks a saving effect, is not the Grace of Christ to whose acknowledgment the Orthodox meant to drive Pelagius. That grace creates the good will, sanctifies the man, and at last infallibly produces salvation’s effect. The Master of the Sentences knew this sense (lib. 2, dist. 26, lit. D): Grace preventing and preparing the will is faith with love. So Aquinas (1a2ae q.111 a.3) when he assigned it five effects: that the soul be healed, will the good, work the good it wills, persevere in the good, and reach glory. Let this stand fixed: received Grace of Christ is not the wage of a non-resisting will; the non-resisting will is the effect of that grace given and received. Enough for the first proposition.
source_text: Quorsum haec tam multa de gratia Christi? Ut intelligatur, Ex communi consensu Orthodoxorum, gratiam illam illuminatricem, monitricem, et excitatricem, quae nulli mortalium deest (si credimus Arminianis) quaeque effectu salutifero in plurimis caret, non esse eam gratiam Christi, ad cujus agnitionem Pelagium adigere Orthodoxi voluerunt; sed eam quae voluntatem bonam creat, hominem sanctificat, ac denique effectum salutis infallibiliter producit. Hunc esse sensum hujus vocabuli non latuit Magistrum Sententiarum, lib. 2. dist. 26. lit. D. Gratia, inquit, voluntatem praeveniens et praeparans, est fides cum dilectione. Hanc etiam gratiam intellexit Aquinas, 1. 2. qu. 111. art. 3. quando quinque effecta ei assignavit, nempe, ut anima sanetur, ut bonum velit, ut bonum quod vult operetur, ut in bono perseveret, ut ad gloriam perveniat. Maneat ergo hoc fixum et stabilitum, Gratiam Christi receptam non esse mercedem voluntatis non-resistentis, sed non-resistentem voluntatem esse effectum hujus gratiae donatae ac receptae. Atque haec ad primae propositionis explicationem abunde sufficiant.
